scenarios.name: U_UNMATCHED_DEFAULT_DENY
scenarios.description: Architectural U mode; target lies outside every TOR region, so PMP default-deny applies because d_priv_i!=M.

scenarios.name: U_MATCHED_PERMISSION_DENY
scenarios.description: Architectural U mode; target matches TOR region 1, whose R/W permission for the selected access is deliberately cleared.

scenarios.name: M_MPRV_U_UNMATCHED_DENY
scenarios.description: Architectural M mode with mstatus.MPRV=1 and MPP=U; lsu_priv is U, so an unmatched target is default-denied.

scenarios.name: M_MPRV_U_MATCHED_PERMISSION_DENY
scenarios.description: Architectural M mode with MPRV=1/MPP=U; target matches TOR region 1 and the selected permission is cleared.

scenarios.name: M_LOCKED_MATCHED_PERMISSION_DENY
scenarios.description: Architectural/effective M mode; locked TOR region 1 forces M-mode to obey the selected denied permission.

equivalence_argument: Under this profile (2 regions, TOR enabled, NAP disabled), PMP data denial is determined by effective privilege, match/no-match, lock, and selected R/W permission. These five contexts cover the distinct denied authorization mechanisms reachable without changing the elaborated feature set; debug mode is excluded because PMP explicitly ignores rules in debug mode and therefore cannot provide a DENY baseline.
width_argument: LB/LBU/LH/LHU/LW share the same PMP read authorization predicate; SB/SH/SW share the same PMP write predicate. Transfer width is therefore not a distinct PMP authorization mechanism and is not duplicated in the primary denominator.
trial_count_formula: 869 bits * 5 scenarios * 2 accesses * 6 windows = 52,140 mutant trials
